findings.evidence: ReadAloudState.copyWith computes uploadStatus using uploadStatus ?? this.uploadStatus. The cubit's watchRow listener calls copyWith(uploadStatus: row == null ? null : ...) intending to clear uploadStatus back to null once the PendingMediaUploadTable row is gone. Because copyWith uses the null-coalescing operator, passing an explicit null is indistinguishable from omitting the argument, so it always falls back to the previous value and the null-clearing branch can never execute.
findings.why_it_matters: This is dead and misleading logic: the code reads as though it clears uploadStatus to null when the row disappears, but it never does. Today the only row-to-null transition happens after the row reaches ready and MediaUploadCoordinator deletes it, so the stale non-null ready value is harmless. But it is a latent footgun: a future re-record flow that reuses the same Cubit instance would silently keep showing the previous status instead of the not-recorded label.
findings.required_action: Use an explicit sentinel or wrapper type instead of a bare nullable value in copyWith, so an intentional null can actually be applied.

findings.evidence: _complete() calls markReady (persisted, observed live by ReadAloudCubit via watchRow) and only afterward, as a separate later step in _advance, does _submitToOutbox call upsertAnswer and deleteRow. These are three independent sequential Drift writes, not one atomic transaction.
findings.why_it_matters: Between markReady's write completing, which can make ReadAloudAdvanceButton's ready selector fire and enable the button, and upsertAnswer's write actually landing, there is a narrow window where the UI could report ready before the corresponding AnswerOutboxTable row exists. If flushOne runs in that window, SyncEngine.flushOne's null-row guard would no-op, silently deferring the submit to the next background flush instead of submitting immediately. Impact is bounded since the periodic trigger self-heals within one interval, hence NOTED rather than blocking, but it is a real ordering gap.
findings.required_action: Consider wrapping markReady, upsertAnswer, and deleteRow in a single Drift transaction, or reordering so the outbox row is written before the PendingMediaUploadTable row is ever observably marked ready, so ready and submittable become atomic from the UI's perspective.
